info.name: WorkDesk24 Task Management APIs
info.description: Task Management endpoints. BASE_URL, TOKEN, ADMIN_TOKEN, and ADMIN_CSRF_TOKEN are resolved from the active Postman environment. Admin requests also require the matching admin CSRF cookie from the admin authentication flow. Run Create Task before requests that use TASK_ID; IDs are saved from successful responses. JSON requests use application/json. Attachment uploads use multipart/form-data so Postman can generate the required boundary.

item.name: Admin APIs
item.description: Admin-only routes under /api/v1/admin/tasks. Uses ADMIN_TOKEN and requires admin CSRF validation.

exec: if (csrf) pm.request.headers.upsert({ key: 'Cookie', value: cookieName + '=' + csrf });

request.description: Returns { status: 'success', timestamp: 'YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm A', data: { columns } } for the authenticated admin's host. Use { hostId: 7 } for all tasks in host 7; every filter is optional. Supports getTasks filters: assignedToUserId (employee), search (task number OR title, trimmed substring, max 100 characters), status (database PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/CANCELLED), priority, createdByUserId, customerId, visitId, dueDate, completedDate, dueFrom/dueTo and overdueOnly. Filters can also be top-level, as in getTasks; nested filters take precedence. Uses the same date validation, host-local calendar-day filtering and allowed sort fields as getTasks. Returns ALL matching tasks without pagination; page/limit do not cap results. Four columns are always present in TODO, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, OVERDUE order with taskCount equal to tasks.length. Deleted/CANCELLED tasks are excluded. PENDING maps to TODO; pending/in-progress tasks with dueAt strictly before the current Unix second appear ONLY in OVERDUE (Overdue SLA). Each card retains its actual database status and the full getTasks task fields, including assignedToUser and createdByUser id/name. dueAt uses the host date format; other timestamps use the host datetime format. Top-level timestamp uses host timezone and the fixed format above. Empty columns return tasks: []. Requires inherited ADMIN_TOKEN and the matching admin CSRF cookie/header. assignedToUserId accepts a single positive ID or an array of positive IDs (for example [47, 48]); array values match ANY selected employee, while all other filters combine with AND. An empty array [] means no employee filter. Duplicate IDs are deduplicated; invalid IDs or array entries return HTTP 400. Required top-level hostId must be a positive safe integer (or digit-only numeric string). Payload/authenticated host matching is temporarily disabled; a different valid payload hostId is accepted but does not change the query scope. Missing/invalid hostId returns HTTP 400 INVALID_HOST_ID. Queries always use the authenticated host, never an untrusted payload scope.

exec: pm.test('Kanban board contract', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(result.status).to.eql('success'); pm.expect(result.timestamp).to.match(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2} (AM|PM)$/); pm.expect(result.data.columns.map(column => column.statusKey)).to.eql(['TODO', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'COMPLETED', 'OVERDUE']); const ids = []; result.data.columns.forEach(column => { pm.expect(column.taskCount).to.eql(column.tasks.length); column.tasks.forEach(task => { ids.push(String(task.id)); pm.expect(task.status).not.to.eql('CANCELLED'); }); }); pm.expect(new Set(ids).size).to.eql(ids.length); });

request.description: All-time task statistics for the authenticated admin's host. A top-level hostId is required; no filters are supported. Other client-supplied identity fields are ignored. Uses inherited ADMIN_TOKEN and matching CSRF cookie/header. Returns { success, message, data: { timestamp, summary, statusDistribution, priorityDistribution, userTasksMetrics } }. timestamp uses the host timezone. statusDistribution contains TODO, IN_PROGRESS, OVERDUE in that order; COMPLETED is excluded. OVERDUE uses color #c00404. summary includes pendingTasks (the non-overdue PENDING count) and overduePercentage (overdue / totalTasks * 100, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 when totalTasks is 0). Deleted and CANCELLED tasks are excluded from all counts. Overdue means a PENDING or IN_PROGRESS task with dueAt strictly before the current Unix second; overdue tasks appear only in OVERDUE, not TODO/IN_PROGRESS. PENDING maps to TODO. Summary percentages use their distribution count / totalTasks * 100 rounded to 2 decimals. User efficiency is completedCount / assignedCount * 100 rounded to 1 decimal. Only users with included assigned tasks are returned, ordered by assignedCount descending then userId ascending, including inactive assignees; deleted or missing user profiles have null name/profileImageUrl while their tasks still count. Empty hosts return zero summary/distribution counts and an empty userTasksMetrics array. priorityDistribution always contains HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, URGENT in that order, each with { priority, label, count, color }. Colors: HIGH #f97316, MEDIUM #3b82f6, LOW #94a3b8, URGENT #ef4444. Priority counts exclude COMPLETED tasks; overdue tasks remain included, and cancelled/deleted tasks are excluded. Empty priorities return count 0. Required top-level hostId must be a positive safe integer (or digit-only numeric string). Payload/authenticated host matching is temporarily disabled; a different valid payload hostId is accepted but does not change the query scope. Missing/invalid hostId returns HTTP 400 INVALID_HOST_ID. Queries always use the authenticated host, never an untrusted payload scope.

exec: pm.test('Dashboard stats response', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(result.success).to.eql(true); pm.expect(result.data.timestamp).to.match(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2} (AM|PM)$/); pm.expect(result.data.summary.pendingTasks).to.be.a('number'); pm.expect(result.data.summary.overduePercentage).to.be.a('number'); pm.expect(result.data.statusDistribution.map(item => item.status)).to.eql(['TODO', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'OVERDUE']); pm.expect(result.data.statusDistribution[2].color).to.eql('#c00404'); pm.expect(result.data.statusDistribution.reduce((total, item) => total + item.count, 0)).to.eql(result.data.summary.pendingTasks + result.data.summary.inProgress + result.data.summary.overdue); pm.expect(result.data.userTasksMetrics).to.be.an('array'); });

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Prepare customer proposal",
  "description": "Draft and review the proposal",
  "assignedToUserId": 22,
  "priority": "HIGH",
  "dueAt": 1791853200
}

request.description: Creates a PENDING task and its CREATED activity log. Replace assignedToUserId with an active field-app user in this tenant. data.task.taskNumber is generated automatically from the authenticated host's settings (default TASK-1, TASK-2, ...). Do not send hostId or taskNumber. A trailing hyphen in the stored prefix is used as the separator; otherwise a hyphen is added. Task, activity log, and counter advancement commit together; failures do not consume a number. Existing host prefixes and counters are preserved.

exec: if (result.success && result.data && result.data.task && result.data.task.id) pm.environment.set('TASK_ID', result.data.task.id);

pm.test('Created task includes an automatic task number', function () { pm.expect(result.success).to.eql(true); pm.expect(result.data.task.taskNumber).to.be.a('string').and.match(/.+-[1-9][0-9]*$/); pm.expect(Array.from(result.data.task.taskNumber).length).to.be.at.most(30); });

request.description: Requires the inherited admin bearer token and matching CSRF cookie/header. Send task fields directly as multipart text fields. title and assignedToUserId are required; description, customerId, visitId, priority, dueAt (Unix seconds), attachment remarks, and the file are optional. Omit the file part to create a task without an attachment, or include one validated JPEG, PNG, WEBP, or PDF file up to 10 MB under file. Do not set Content-Type manually. Returns data.task and includes data.attachment only when a file is uploaded. The server links the attachment to the newly created task; do not send taskId or taskCommentId. Task, activity, counter, and attachment metadata commit together; failures roll back and attempt uploaded-file cleanup. Notifications run only after commit. The separate creation and upload endpoints remain available.

exec: pm.test('Task is created and attachment is optional', function () { pm.expect(result.success).to.eql(true); pm.expect(result.data.task).to.be.an('object'); if (result.data.attachment) pm.expect(String(result.data.attachment.taskId)).to.eql(String(result.data.task.id)); });

request.description: Filters also support assignedToUserId, createdByUserId, customerId, visitId, dueDate and completedDate. Date filters are optional YYYY-MM-DD or DD/MM/YYYY strings, for example filters: { dueDate: '2026-10-23', completedDate: '23/10/2026' }. Formats can be mixed in one request. Each date is interpreted in the authenticated client's configured host timezone (HostSettings timezone), the same timezone used for response formatting, and converted to inclusive start/end-of-day Unix seconds for dueAt/completedAt comparisons, including DST. Both filters combine with AND. Omit unused date filters; null, timestamps and invalid dates return HTTP 400. Legacy dueFrom/dueTo Unix-second bounds remain supported but cannot be combined with dueDate. Success retains { success, message, data: { tasks, pagination } }. assignedToUserId accepts a single positive ID or an array of positive IDs (for example [47, 48]); array values match ANY selected employee, while all other filters combine with AND. An empty array [] means no employee filter. Duplicate IDs are deduplicated; invalid IDs or array entries return HTTP 400.

Returns task details with up to 10 recent comments, attachments, and activity records. Each comment includes an attachments array containing attachments linked to that comment; task-level attachments remain in task.attachments.

body.raw:
{
  "taskId": {{TASK_ID}},
  "title": "Prepare revised customer proposal",
  "description": "Update the pricing section and review",
  "priority": "URGENT",
  "dueAt": 1791856800
}

exec: if (result.success && result.data && result.data.comment && result.data.comment.id) pm.environment.set('COMMENT_ID', result.data.comment.id);

request.description: Creates a task comment and optionally its linked attachment atomically. Requires taskId and comment (1-5000 characters). Omit the file part to add a comment without an attachment, or include one JPEG, PNG, WEBP, or PDF file up to 10 MB. Optional remarks: up to 500 characters. Uses inherited ADMIN_TOKEN bearer authentication and the matching admin CSRF cookie/header. Postman sets the multipart Content-Type boundary. Success always returns data.comment and includes data.attachment only when a file is uploaded; attachment.taskCommentId is the newly created comment ID. Uploaded media is deleted if persistence fails.

Choose a JPEG, PNG, WEBP, or PDF file no larger than 10 MB. Postman will set the multipart Content-Type with its boundary. The response data.attachment.fileName preserves normal filename characters and replaces path separators and control characters. Open data.attachment.fileUrl exactly as returned, including its authenticated Cloudinary signature and file extension. Cloudinary must allow PDF delivery in the account security settings.

exec: if (result.success && result.data && result.data.attachment && result.data.attachment.id) pm.environment.set('ATTACHMENT_ID', result.data.attachment.id);

item.name: App APIs
item.description: Employee task routes under /api/v1/app/task. Uses TOKEN from the active Postman environment. Employees can only access tasks assigned to them.

request.description: Uses inherited employee bearer authentication. Optional filters.dueDate and filters.completedDate accept YYYY-MM-DD or DD/MM/YYYY, for example 2026-10-23 or 23/10/2026. Formats can be mixed in one request. The server uses the client's configured host timezone (HostSettings timezone) to compare inclusive local-day Unix-second bounds against dueAt/completedAt. Both filters combine with AND; omit unused filters. Invalid dates and null return HTTP 400. Legacy dueFrom/dueTo Unix bounds remain supported but cannot be combined with dueDate. Employees still see only their assigned tasks. Success retains { success, message, data: { tasks, pagination } }.

Returns task details with up to 10 recent comments, attachments, and activity records. Each comment includes an attachments array containing attachments linked to that comment; task-level attachments remain in task.attachments.

exec: if (result.success && result.data && result.data.comment && result.data.comment.id) pm.environment.set('COMMENT_ID', result.data.comment.id);

request.description: Choose a JPEG, PNG, WEBP, or PDF file no larger than 10 MB. Postman sets the multipart Content-Type boundary automatically. The response data.attachment.fileName preserves normal filename characters and replaces path separators and control characters. Open data.attachment.fileUrl exactly as returned, including its authenticated Cloudinary signature and file extension. Cloudinary must allow PDF delivery in the account security settings.

exec: if (result.success && result.data && result.data.attachment && result.data.attachment.id) pm.environment.set('ATTACHMENT_ID', result.data.attachment.id);

request.description: Inherits the app Bearer TOKEN. Use Send and Download: HTTP 200 contains raw PDF/JPEG/PNG/WEBP bytes, not JSON. Requires a same-host, non-deleted task assigned to this user or same-host admin access; a linked comment must exist on that task. Errors use the standard JSON format: 400 invalid ID, 401 invalid authentication, 404 inaccessible/missing attachment/task/comment, 502 unavailable/untrusted upstream asset, 504 upstream timeout. No Cloudinary redirect or URL is returned by this endpoint.

exec: pm.test('Response is an attachment, not a redirect', () => { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Disposition')).to.match(/^attachment;/); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.has('Location')).to.eql(false); });
